title: The quiz: the first three questions
one: Get to the quiz, then mark a typed answer, two buttons and a list.

next.title: The quiz: questions 4 and 5, and the score

screens.title: Check what your quiz already has
screens.goal: I check for the quiz form and its six panels, the Take quiz button, and the marking of questions 1, 2 and 3.

blocks.p: Your quiz may be partly made already. This screen checks what is there.

check.what: Is frmQuiz in Solution Explorer? Does it hold a score panel and five question panels?
check.how: Double-click frmQuiz in Solution Explorer. It opens in the Design tab.

check.what: Does question 4 have four round buttons and a Check button? Does question 5 have a number box?
check.how: Click each control once. Its name shows near the top of Properties.

check.what: Run it. Does the Take quiz button open the quiz?
check.how: Use the green Start arrow. Log in and fill in the data entry form first.

check.what: Answer question 1 and press Check. Does its panel turn green or red?
check.how: Green means right. Red means wrong.

check.what: Do question 2's buttons and question 3's list mark the answer?
check.how: Try each one. The panel should turn green or red.

stages.title: The quiz form: its panels and buttons

screens.title: Add the quiz form and its six panels
screens.goal: I add a form called frmQuiz and put six panels on it, each named for what it holds.

blocks.p: The quiz is a form of its own. It holds a score panel and five question panels.

steps.do: Click the Project menu along the top. Click the line that starts Add Form.
steps.see: A box opens with Form picked in its list.
wrong: Click your project's name in Solution Explorer first. Then open the Project menu again.

steps.do: In the Name box at the bottom, type frmQuiz.cs. Click Add.
steps.see: frmQuiz opens in the Design tab. It is empty.

steps.do: Drag six panels from the Toolbox onto it. Name each one as the map shows.
steps.see: Six panels, each with a name that starts with pnl.

frames.alt: The Project menu open, with Add Form in its list
frames.say: Open the Project menu. Click the line that starts Add Form.

frames.alt: The Add New Item box with Form picked and a name in the Name box
frames.say: Form is picked. Type the form's name in the Name box.

frames.alt: The new empty form in the Design tab
frames.say: Click Add. The new form opens in the Design tab. My picture says frmTemp. Yours shows the name you typed.

flow.say: Six panels. One holds the score. Each of the other five holds one question.

blocks.p: Each panel is named for what is in it, not a number. So YOUR quiz can put its questions in any order.

screens.title: Fill the score panel and the question 1 panel
screens.goal: The score panel holds the title, the score, a comment and two buttons, and question 1 holds a label, a box and Check.

blocks.p: Drag each control into its panel. Then give it its name and its Text.

rows.name: lblComment
set: Text = a line to start the quiz

controls.done: The first six sit inside pnlQuizScore. The last three sit inside pnlTextQuestion.

blocks.yours: MY questions are about water safety. Type YOUR five questions into the Text of each question label.

screens.title: Fill the question 2 and question 3 panels
screens.goal: Question 2 holds a label and two answer buttons, and question 3 holds a label, a picture, a list and Check.

blocks.p: Question 2 is answered with one of two buttons. Question 3 is answered from a drop-down list.

rows.name: cbxQuestion3
set: Items = the choices, one per line

controls.done: The first three sit inside pnlButtonsQuestion. The last four sit inside pnlListQuestion.

blocks.p: In the Toolbox, PictureBox makes a picture box. ComboBox makes a drop-down list.
For Image, click the three dots beside it. Click Import, pick YOUR picture, then click OK.
Items works as it did for the year group list in chapter 2.

blocks.watch: Put the RIGHT answer first in the Items list. The code on screen 5-4 looks for it there.

screens.title: Fill the question 4 and question 5 panels
screens.goal: Question 4 holds a group box with four round buttons and Check, and question 5 holds a label, a number box and Check.

blocks.p: Question 4 has four answers. Only one can be picked. Question 5 is answered with a number.

frames.title: Drag a group box, round buttons and a number box

frames.say: Drag a GroupBox into the question 4 panel.

frames.alt: Four RadioButtons dropped inside the group box
frames.say: Drag four RadioButtons INSIDE the group box.

frames.alt: A NumericUpDown dropped into the question 5 panel
frames.say: Drag a NumericUpDown into the question 5 panel.

controls.done: The group box sits in pnlRadioQuestion, with the next five inside it. The last three sit inside pnlNumberQuestion.

blocks.watch: The four round buttons and btnCheck4 go INSIDE the group box. Then only one round button can be picked.

screens.title: Open the quiz from the Take quiz button
screens.goal: Pressing Take quiz closes the data entry form and opens a new quiz form.

blocks.p: The Take quiz button is on the data entry form. It swaps that form for the quiz.

words: Make a new quiz form and show it.
Turn every letter into a small letter.
The background colour of a control.
blocks.intro: Four new things in this chapter. Two are on this screen. Click one to see what it means.

drawn.alt: The data entry form fades away. The quiz form appears in its place.
drawn.say: The data entry form closes. The quiz form opens.

steps.do: Open frmDataEntry in the Design tab. Double-click the Take quiz button.
steps.see: The code tab opens at btnTakeQuiz_Click.

code.title: The Take quiz button
code.where: between the curly brackets of btnTakeQuiz_Click
partLines: Visual Studio wrote these two lines
Leave them as they are. Your code goes between the curly brackets.
given
Close this form, open the quiz
A note for you. The data entry form closes. A new quiz form opens.
Visual Studio wrote this line
This curly bracket is the end. Your code goes above it.
given

blocks.p: [[this.Close()|0]] closes the data entry form. [[new frmQuiz().Show()|1]] makes the quiz and shows it.

blocks.watch: The data entry form forgets everything when it closes. So its details are kept in Global.cs.

screens.title: Mark the typed answer to question 1 right or wrong
screens.goal: If the typed answer in small letters matches, the score goes up and the panel turns green, or else it turns red.

blocks.p: Question 1 is typed in a box. Its Check button marks it.
[[.ToLower()|2]] turns every letter small. So EMERGENCY and Emergency both match.
[[BackColor|3]] is the background colour of a panel. Green means right. Red means wrong.

steps.do: Open frmQuiz in the Design tab. Double-click the Check button of question 1.
steps.see: The code tab opens at btnCheck1_Click.

code.title: Question 1's Check button, part 1 of 2
code.where: between the curly brackets of btnCheck1_Click
partLines: Visual Studio wrote these two lines
Leave them as they are. Your code goes between the curly brackets.
given
Right?
Is the answer, in small letters, emergency? Then add 1, turn the panel green and show the score.
Wrong
Any other answer turns the panel red.
code.yours: MY answer is emergency. Type YOUR answer, all in small letters.

screens.title: Switch off question 1 and switch on question 2
screens.goal: After question 1 is marked, its panel switches off and the question 2 panel switches on.

blocks.p: Right or wrong, the quiz moves on. Question 1 switches off. Question 2 switches on.

flow.say: The question 1 panel switches off. The question 2 panel switches on.

code.title: Question 1's Check button, part 2 of 2
code.where: under part 1, inside btnCheck1_Click, in frmQuiz.cs
partLines: Move to the next question
Question 1 switches off. Question 2 switches on.
Visual Studio wrote these two lines
Leave them as they are. Your code goes between the curly brackets.
given

blocks.watch: Type these two lines straight after the last line of part 1. They run for a right answer and a wrong one.

screens.title: Score a point when the right button is pressed
screens.goal: The right answer button adds 1 to the score, turns the panel green and switches on question 3.

blocks.p: Question 2 has two buttons. Each button has its own code. Only the right button adds a point.

steps.do: In the Design tab, double-click the right answer button of question 2.
steps.see: The code tab opens at btnCorrect_Click.

code.title: The right answer button
code.where: between the curly brackets of btnCorrect_Click
partLines: Visual Studio wrote these two lines

given
Add a point
A note for you. Then 1 is added to the score, and the score is shown.

The panel turns green. Question 2 switches off. Question 3 switches on.

code.yours: Which of YOUR two buttons is the right answer? Only that one scores.

screens.title: Turn question 2 red when the wrong button is pressed
screens.goal: The wrong answer button turns the panel red, adds nothing, and still switches on question 3.

blocks.p: The wrong button does the same, with two changes. It adds no point, and the panel turns red.

steps.do: In the Design tab, double-click the wrong answer button of question 2.
steps.see: The code tab opens at btnIncorrect_Click.

screens.title: Stop question 3 when nothing is chosen
screens.goal: If nothing is chosen in the question 3 list, a message asks the user to choose and nothing else happens.

blocks.p: Question 3 is a drop-down list. A user could press Check with nothing chosen.
.SelectedIndex == -1 asks if nothing is chosen. You met it in chapter 4.

steps.do: In the Design tab, double-click the Check button of question 3.
steps.see: The code tab opens at btnCheck3_Click.

code.title: Question 3's Check button, part 1 of 3
code.where: between the curly brackets of btnCheck3_Click
partLines: Visual Studio wrote these two lines
Leave them as they are. Your code goes between the curly brackets.
given
Nothing chosen?
If nothing is chosen, a note for you, then a message asks the user to choose.

blocks.watch: With nothing chosen, nothing else happens. The list stays switched on so the user can choose.

screens.title: Score a point when the right item is chosen
screens.goal: If the first item in the list is chosen, the score goes up and the panel turns green.

blocks.p: else runs when something is chosen. Then the code asks: is it the right item?
The items are counted from 0. So the first item is number 0.

code.title: Question 3's Check button, part 2 of 3
partLines: Something is chosen
else, then its curly bracket.
Right?
Is item 0 chosen? A note, then add 1, turn the panel green and show the score.
code.yours: MY right answer is the first item in the list, number 0. Count YOUR list from 0.

screens.goal: Any other item turns the panel red, then question 3 switches off and question 4 switches on.

blocks.p: Last, a wrong item turns the panel red. Then the quiz moves on to question 4.

screens.title: Try every way through questions 1, 2 and 3
screens.goal: I open the quiz, answer in capitals, answer wrongly, try both kinds of button, and press Check with nothing chosen.

blocks.p: Run your program and get to the Take quiz button. Then try each row.

check.how: The data entry form closes. The quiz opens.

check.what: Type YOUR question 1 answer in capitals. Press Check.
check.how: The panel goes green. The score shows 1.

check.what: Run it again. Type a wrong answer for question 1. Press Check.
check.how: The panel goes red. Question 2 can be clicked.

check.what: Press the right button for question 2.
check.how: The panel goes green and the score goes up by 1.

check.what: Choose nothing in the list and press Check.
check.how: A message asks you to choose. The quiz must NOT move on to question 4.
check.fix: If it moved on, look at screen 5-3.
